title: The Kurma Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa like the other Puranas. The Kūrma Purāṇa is a Shaiva compilation, mainly of northern origin, that has taken in Vaishnava and Shakta material as well; its two parts, pūrva and uttara, were formed at different times.
description: The Kūrma Purāṇa is spoken by Vishnu in his tortoise form to the king Indradyumna and then to the sages: it tells the creation and the four ages, the genealogy of the gods and kings, the sacred places of the earth and the duties of the castes and the stages of life, and then the Śiva chapter, in which Shiva declares himself the one to be known and worshipped. Its second part turns to the teaching of release, to the terrible goddesses and their worship, and to the doctrines of the Śaiva schools in a summary that has made the text important for the history of Shaiva thought.
historicalContext: The Purana's Śiva-gītā is quoted by the Śaiva Siddhānta as one of its scriptural authorities, and its chapters on the sacred sites of the Narmada and the north give the pilgrim geography of the Shaiva traditions; it was also used by the compilers of later legal and ritual digests.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the whole Purāṇa in its two parts, 96 chapters and 5,823 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time. Each passage is one verse, addressed as part.chapter.verse; the auspicious opening, which the edition numbers separately and lettered, forms the first chapter of part one.
